metadata.topic: Gas Laws — Gradient of Pressure-Temperature Graph (Pressure Law Experiment)
metadata.note: Data: P (×10⁵ Pa) = {1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7} at θ (°C) = {25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150}. Data is perfectly linear. Gradient = ΔP/Δθ = 0.5×10⁵/125 = 4000 Pa/°C = 4.0×10² Pa°C⁻¹. Follows Q1b (plotting — not auto-gradeable). Q1b(ii) (absolute zero extrapolation) and Q1d (pressure law statement — DDWTOS) are in separate files.

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q1c — Gradient of P vs θ Graph
question.text:
An experiment investigates how the pressure of a fixed mass of gas varies with temperature. Results from Table 1 are shown below:

Pressure P / (×10⁵ Pa)Temperature θ / °C
1.225.0
1.350.0
1.475.0
1.5100.0
1.6125.0
1.7150.0

Use the graph to determine the gradient of the line. (5 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Model gradient (using extreme points):
ΔP = (1.7 − 1.2) × 10⁵ = 0.5 × 10⁵ Pa
Δθ = 150 − 25 = 125 °C
Gradient = ΔP/Δθ = 0.5 × 10⁵ / 125 = 4.0 × 10² Pa °C⁻¹ (400 Pa/°C)

Since the data is perfectly linear, any two well-separated data points (or graph readings) yield the same gradient.

steps.label:
Gradient formula: G = ΔP/Δθ (rise over run: change in pressure ÷ change in temperature)
Units: ΔP in Pa (or ×10⁵ Pa)  |  Δθ in °C  |  Choose two well-separated points on the best-fit line
Calculate the gradient of the P vs θ graph using two well-separated points. (5 marks)

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Choose two points far apart on the line of best fit. ΔP = upper pressure − lower pressure from your chosen pair.
Δθ = the difference in temperature values for your two chosen points on the best-fit line.

fields.label: Gradient G = ΔP/Δθ = _____ × 10² Pa °C⁻¹
fields.diagnostic_hint: G = 0.5×10⁵ / 125 = 4.0×10² Pa/°C (i.e., 400 Pa per degree Celsius)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: G = ΔP ÷ Δθ = (0.5 × 10⁵) ÷ 125 = 4.0 × 10² Pa/°C. Divide the change in pressure by the change in temperature.
